title: Forum shopping
summary: Forum shopping is choosing a court in light of advantages that the forum’s rules, governing law, or procedures may offer. It becomes legally significant when a doctrine seeks to prevent particular incentives or unfair differences.
notes: Choosing a permitted forum is not inherently unlawful. The doctrinal consequence depends on the specific jurisdictional, governing-law, or transfer rule.

sections.Meaning: Forum shopping is choosing a court in light of advantages that the forum’s rules, governing law, or procedures may offer. It becomes legally significant when a doctrine seeks to prevent particular incentives or unfair differences.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the available forums and the advantage sought. Erie and Hanna focus on differences arising from the federal rather than state forum; venue and transfer address other aspects of forum choice. Explain the particular incentive rather than labeling every strategic choice improper.
